1.א: “And if shogeg”—see Beur Halakhah; “also one who forgot” is from Responsa Maharam Mintz §28; see Sha’arei Ephraim siman 28 and Shevus Yaakov II §128 and above §108; see Ba’er Heiteiv.

2.ב: On Shabbat—Beur Halakhah there; regarding vessels—people routinely rule kasher for Pesach by hagalah three times as explained in YD there.

3.ג: Insulating—Beur Halakhah; see Novellae Megillah 23 that pickled “like roasting” absorbs like earthenware for kashering—but whether it counts as “roasted” for Shabbat bishul or forbidding Pesach salted as “roasted” because of safek—see there.

5.ד: Cooking—Beur Halakhah; see Gilyon Maharsha §19 Responsa Maharas Ḥiwvan that if keli sheni has only water it is forbidden to put ground coffee because appearance changes (like dyeing) and pesik reisha—especially keli rishon one would fear chatat; but if coffee contains enough moisture to soak then keli sheni not forbidden—see there.

9.ה: Nullification—Beur Halakhah; see Pri Megadim §84 those who bring Shabbat hot water in keli rishon—if mistakenly pours keli rishon into small bowls with sugar no bishul because sugar was cooked at factory and dry food has no bishul aḥar bishul even when dissolved—like Magen Avraham on salt; Mishnah Berurah cites Zera Emet who hesitates and concludes better to pour coffee into cups then add sugar—obviously only when keli rishon is boiling and yad soledes bo.

15.ו: Cooled—see Beur Halakhah; see Rav Yosef in name of Mahari Trani manuscript custom in Constantinople that maids place milieu/trindle to warm in oven Shabbat morning before eating—now challenged from BY §253—seems permitted from elsewhere… poultry without gravy all permit; no difference oven versus opposite fire since side-opening oven is like room—not worse than opposite fire; sealing oven only keeps heat… Mayim Rabim §21 permits leaning on oven even with some congealed fat but much gravy forbidden because dish improves (metzamek) on Shabbat; also his view forbids warming in oven or kirah even fully cooked if metzamek ve-ra lo—looks like cooking since that’s normal cooking; not near fire or opposite fire where not normal—practice is lenient especially where ovens aren’t used for cooking only keeping water hot; soup with meat Shabbat morning placed far from oven heat near door seal—not yad soledes; where yad soledes forbidden because gravy fully cooled—see §253 §16 Taz. See Kenesset HaGedolah §17—coffee cooked may be opposite fire even by Jew but on flame forbidden even via Gentile or himself—see there.

16.ז: “Some are stringent”—Beur Halakhah; see §84 disagreeing with Magen Avraham—holds even where yad soledes bedieved no issur; where no yad soledes permitted lechatchilah pashtida—even if practice stringent it may be mistaken custom—see there.
